title: Global State vs. a Fresh Environment
description: The BAD version keeps one dictionary and mutates it in place; the GOOD version creates a fresh Environment on every call.

steps.description: This shows the global-state mistake and its fix. The page repeats it in Part 7 because it is the most common cause of mysterious, order-dependent test failures.
The `BAD` version keeps one dictionary, `_env`, and `run` modifies it in place, so a binding from one call survives into the next.
The `GOOD` version creates a fresh `Environment()` for every call and passes it to `evaluate`. The page says a fresh environment per call isolates every test automatically.

steps.question: The page says if you use the `pytest-randomly` plugin, which flag restores a fixed order while you isolate the problem?
